title: Reliability launchpad: Crossbeam charter & sprint checklist
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact launchpad charter for a cross-functional reliability sprint (Crossbeam) to operationalize SLOs for high-traffic model-serving routes. Goal is a 6-week cadence that produces: clear SLO definitions, alert-to-runbook mappings, a lightweight dashboard for product owners, and an ops handoff for oncall coverage.

Scope (what's in/out):
- IN: 3 critical model-serving routes (text-generation-api, chat-stream, embeddings-batch), definition and measurement of latency and error-rate SLOs, first-pass dashboards, alert mapping, and a single canary rollout that exercises fallback routing.
- OUT: full-service-level contracts with legal, billing-level penalties, deep instrumentation on every microservice (future work).

Principles:
- Keep SLOs pragmatic: start with one latency percentile and one availability metric per route.
- Make dashboards usable by product owners (no raw PromQL).
- Prefer guardrails and graceful degradation (fallback model variants) over strict blocking.
- Lean runbooks: two-page oncall steps + links to detailed diagnostics.

Stakeholders & Roles:
- Program lead: Priya Shah (SRE) — overall program coordination
- Product partner: Evelyn Tran (product-hosted-api) — SLO business acceptance
- Serving runtime lead: Marcus Lee (serving-runtime) — measurement and instrumentation
- Observability engineer: Diego Ramirez (observability) — dashboards and alert rules
- Solutions eng: Kara N. — customer impact assessment / beta customer liaison

Success criteria (by end of sprint):
1) SLO definitions agreed for the three routes (latency p95, p99; availability 99.9% target for critical path) and recorded in Confluence.
2) Dashboards with traffic, SLO status, and top-3 contributing error classes live in Redwood Console for the team.
3) Alerts map to a documented runbook (triage, mitigation, rollback) and one automation to route a degraded request to fallback model is validated in staging.
4) Oncall rotation updated and a 1-hour tabletop executed with product & support.

Draft SLOs (starting point, up for discussion):
- text-generation-api: latency p95 < 220 ms (for 512 tokens), availability >= 99.95%
- chat-stream: tail latency p99 < 400 ms, availability >= 99.9% (streaming-specific errors counted)
- embeddings-batch: throughput SLO (batch completion within SLA) 95% of batches < 30s, availability >=99.8%

Metrics & Sources:
- Latency/error metrics: telemetry from serving-runtime (prometheus labels: route, model_variant, quantization_profile)
- Traffic: request volume, model size, sequence length distribution (sampled histogram)
- User impact signals: error reports, 5xx uplift, alpha customer tickets

Dashboards: minimal views to build by week 2
- Overview: SLO status cards per route, daily burn rate, active incidents
- Signal drill-down: p50/p95/p99 latency histograms, error taxonomy, hot endpoints
- Canary view: requests routed to fallback, success rate, latency delta

Alerting (high level):
- Page when burn rate > 2x sustained for 30m OR availability breach > 1m
- P2 notification to product slack channel when canary fails >10% requests in 5m
- Alert payloads must include quick links: runbook, recent deploys (git commit), top traces

Runbook skeleton (one-pager):
- Priority assessment: is this customer-impacting? Check SLO card + alpha tickets.
- Quick mitigation: switch routing policy to fallback-variant (runbook CLI snippet), reduce batch size, enable circuit-breaker for non-critical endpoints.
- If mitigation reduces error rate --> follow rollback and postmortem flow.
- Escalation: notify product lead and solutions eng if mitigation fails after 20m.

Risk & Dependencies:
- Dependency: telemetry must tag model_variant consistently — serving-runtime owners to deliver by Week 1. (Risk: missing labels -> noisy metrics)
- Dependency: dashboard templating in Console needs small SDK change (PR #189) to embed SLO cards.
- Risk: customer-facing regressions if Canary fallback not validated; plan a staged canary with low percentage traffic.

Timeline & 6-week cadence (high level):
- Week 0 (alignment): stakeholder kickoff, baseline metrics capture, agree SLO drafts.
- Week 1: instrumentation changes, metrics schema locked, dashboard scaffold.
- Week 2: dashboards live in staging, initial alert rules, runbook draft.
- Week 3: run tabletop exercise, iterate SLO thresholds with product.
- Week 4: deploy canary fallback in staging, run chaos tests for degradation scenarios.
- Week 5: validate rollback & automation, finalize dashboards and handoff materials.
- Week 6: production canary (limited), final sign-off, retro & next steps.

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Which SLA tiers should be backed by Dedicated capacity (suggestion: text-generation-api critical customers)?
- Burn rate threshold sensitivity for streaming endpoints — product input needed.
- Exact tagging format for model_variant label (proposal: model_repo@sha:variant).

Communications & Cadence:
- Weekly 30m stakeholder sync (Mon 10:00 PT)
- Daily 15m triage during canary weeks
- Slack channel: #reliability-crossbeam-launch (ops + product + serving)

Artifacts to produce (deliverables):
- Confluence doc with chosen SLOs and acceptance criteria (link in linked_artifacts)
- Console dashboard templates + JSON export
- One-page runbooks per route (stored in runbooks/ dir)
- Post-mortem template and incident playbook updated to reference SLOs

Next steps (this week):
- Marcus to land metric labels PR by Thu EOD (blocking).
- Diego to scaffold dashboard JSON and share on staging workspace by Fri.
- Product to review draft SLO targets (Evelyn) — comment by Wed.

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider automated SLO tuning agent in Optimize later: start with manual thresholds but capture burn-rate curves for ML later.
- Could add a lightweight customer opt-in for Canary testing (beta customers) to increase confidence.
- Save a template for runbook CLI snippets that can be copy-pasted into alerts.

Appendix: quick references
- Related JIRA: JIRA-INF-3421 (telemetry labels), JIRA-INF-3478 (canary routing automation)
- Observability PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/189

-- end of draft --
